audit_rationale: Candidate B's memorandum integrates two hypothetical scientists' evidence pools and generally cites plausible, topically relevant abstracts for its central mechanistic claims (interfacial contact bottlenecks, tortuosity/lithiation gradients, chemical instability at the NCM-LPSCl interface, and the benefit of mixed/bimodal SE particle sizing). This produces meaningful uncertainty in mapping several claims (especially C1 and C3) to a uniquely resolvable record, lowering citation traceability. No claim is contradicted by supplied evidence, and no clearly fabricated identifier was found, but the dual-pool ambiguity for shared numeric IDs (20, 5) creates genuine uncertainty about whether the candidate's own internal labeling reliably resolves the pool ambiguity as required by the audit rules.
uncertainty_notes: The candidate's use of 'Scientist A [ID: n]' vs 'Scientist B [ID: n]' appears intended to disambiguate pool A vs pool B, and in most cases the labels do align with the supplied pool tags (e.g., Scientist B [ID:20] maps to pool B record B-R01b). I flagged fabricated_or_invalid_citation_identifier as uncertain rather than yes/no because no identifier is clearly invalid or nonexistent (all cited IDs have corresponding abstracts), but the dual-pool ID collisions (20, 5) leave some doubt about unique attribution for a subset of citations.

No claim is directly contradicted, but the core architectural synthesis (Mo-Ni dual-metal sulfide with dual-carbon and Kirkendall-void engineering) is not demonstrated as an integrated system in any single cited abstract, so I flag the consequential-unsupported-claim item as uncertain rather than outright yes, since the individual sub-mechanisms (Kirkendall voids, rGO buffering, carbon-matrix binding, spray-drying scalability) are each independently supported by literature, just not in combination for this exact chemistry.

The genuinely novel Mo-Ni multicomponent chalcogenide system proposed is not itself the subject of any supplied abstract, which is inherent to a forward-looking design memo and is reflected in the widespread 'partially_supported' ratings rather than 'unsupported' or 'contradicted', since analogous systems do lend plausibility without being directly on-point.
